sources.entry: fabric - A simple, Pythonic tool for remote execution and deployment.

summary.one_liner: Fabric is a Python library for executing shell commands on remote machines over SSH and getting useful Python objects back.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Fabric as a high-level Python library (supporting Python 2.7 and 3.4+) for running shell commands remotely over SSH. It is built on top of Invoke, which handles subprocess command execution and command-line features, and Paramiko, which implements the SSH protocol. Fabric extends those APIs so they work together and adds further functionality. The README links to a changelog for new-version details and to a maintainer roadmap. It does not detail specific deployment commands or API examples in the text provided.
use_cases: running shell commands on remote servers over SSH
scripting administration tasks on remote machines
notable: Built on Invoke for command execution and Paramiko for the SSH protocol
Returns useful Python objects from remote command execution
Supports Python 2.7 and 3.4+ according to the README
caveats: The README provided is short and does not include installation or usage instructions
Python 2.7 support is listed, which is outdated
